title: Introduce self-service Cost Attribution connector + priority gating for enterprise dashboard requests
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Problem statement: Enterprise customers frequently request ad-hoc cost breakdowns and joined analytics across multiple workspaces and routes. Current console flows and one-off exports require manual triage, engineering pull requests, or custom reports, creating long lead times and inconsistent deliverables. This ticket defines a product play to enable a self-serve 'Cost Attribution' connector that (a) streams deterministic per-route/per-feature cost attribution to a customer data sink (S3/BigQuery/CSV), (b) surfaces an intake + priority-gating flow in the Console for enterprise requests, and (c) provides standard dashboard templates and a lightweight SLA for delivery and support.

Scope and non-goals: Scope covers the intake rubric, priority lanes, connector spec (schema + retention), and two dashboard templates (team-level and tenant-level). Engineering work for the connector runtime/ETL and RBAC/invoice mapping live in ENG dependencies. Non-goals: building a full BI product, complex chargeback UI, or replacing existing billing exports.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form in Console that captures enterprise context, urgency, data destination (S3/BQ/CSV), and required cost dimension (workspace, route, model-version, feature-flag)
Priority gating algorithm documented and enforced: SLA lanes (Standard: 10 business days, High: 3 business days) with eligibility checks against customer tier and contractual entitlements
Connector spec v1 (schema, encryption/KMS, PII redaction rules, retention policy) published and signed off by Security & Legal
Two dashboard templates available in console: Workspace-level 'Cost by Route' and Org-level 'Cross-workspace Attribution' with example queries
Operational playbook created: triage runbook, escalation path, and metrics to track (time-to-delivery, request backlog, %auto-fulfilled)
comments: 2026-02-02 - Asha Mehta: Initial intake from sales (ACME Corp) requesting monthly cost breakdown by route + model variant across 6 workspaces. They need CSV sink to S3 and a monthly cadence. Marking as P1 due to enterprise contract clause.

2026-02-04 - Liam O'Connor: Met with infra and ENG leads (ENG-3912). We should reuse existing telemetry export path but add route/model_variant fields. Engineering flagged RBAC + KMS integration as dependencies.
2026-02-06 - Security (Marta Ruiz): High-level connector spec accepted, but must include field-level redaction and audit logs. Security review required before customer-facing GA.
2026-02-09 - Solutions Eng (Rajat Singh): Customer success needs sample S3 + BQ templates and a 'smoke-check' report to validate the mapping. Added as acceptance criteria.

2026-02-12 - Product Review: Prioritization discussion - propose auto-fulfillment for customers on Dedicated or Private tiers; self-serve for hosted customers with sufficient usage. Waiting on legal review for data destination contracts.

2026-02-14 - Liam O'Connor: Updated dependencies to include ENG-4060 (billing-schema normalization). Draft PRD uploaded (see links). Next: confirm storage cost model with finance and finalize SLA language.
rollout_steps: Phase 0: Finalize PRD, connector schema, and security sign-off (owner: PM)
Phase 1: Engineering to deliver v0 connector and auto-fulfillment path for Dedicated customers (owner: ENG)
Phase 2: Expose intake UI and priority gating in Console; surface eligibility and SLA estimates (owner: Console UX)
Phase 3: Pilot with 3 enterprise customers (CS + Solutions Eng), collect feedback and measure time-to-delivery
Phase 4: Open self-serve for hosted customers that meet usage thresholds and pass onboarding checklist
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: Keep initial schema narrow (workspace, route, model_variant, tokens, cost) to ship quickly vs. supporting arbitrary user tags. Decision: narrow for v1, add extensibility hooks for v2.

Tradeoff: Auto-fulfill requests for Dedicated/Private to reduce engineer load vs. manual approvals to ensure compliance. Decision: auto-fulfill for Dedicated/Private; manual gating for Hosted until we validate cost model.
Tradeoff: Real-time streaming vs. periodic batch exports. Decision: start with daily batch exports (easier for KMS/audit) and evaluate streaming after pilot.
Risk: Long-tail requests that require joins with customer-side event stores. Mitigation: surface clear limits and offer paid Professional Services for custom joins.
